html:
The Battle of the Little Bighorn was fought on 25 and 26 June 1876 in Montana, where Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors destroyed five companies of the US 7th Cavalry under George Armstrong Custer. It is the best known battle of the wars on the Plains.

The cause was the Black Hills. The Fort Laramie treaty of 1868 had kept them for the Lakota, but after Custer's own expedition reported gold there in 1874, miners poured in, and the US ordered all bands onto reservations. Many refused and gathered with Sitting Bull of the Hunkpapa in a huge camp on the Little Bighorn River. Crow and Arikara scouts guided the army.

Custer split his regiment and attacked. Major Reno's men were driven back onto a hilltop, and Custer and every man with him, more than two hundred, were killed. Leaders on the Native side included Crazy Horse of the Oglala and Gall of the Hunkpapa.

The victory changed little. The army hunted the bands down through the next winter. Crazy Horse surrendered in 1877, and Sitting Bull fled to Canada. The US took the Black Hills in 1877; in 1980 the Supreme Court ruled the taking unjust, and the Lakota have refused the money.
